text:
Mark Kastelic is the Bruins' fourth-line enforcer who can also play, and the team has leaned on that edge this fall: NHL.com's Sunday read went inside the anatomy of a fight with him and Tanner Jeannot. He plays about 11 minutes a night, hits often (43 in 21 games) and blocks shots.

The offense is honest. He has 3 goals and 7 points, almost exactly what his chances say he should have, and his rate of chances is ahead of last season's 12-goal pace. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains how he gets them: 56% of his shots come off the rush, and he rarely carries the puck into the zone, so his line lives on dump-ins and turnovers.

The cold stretch is the part to watch. He has one goal in his last ten games while his ice time has dipped, and Boston has lost three straight. His plays-like matches, grinders like Morgan Barron and Michael McCarron, share a flag that also shows up for him: chances against tend to pile up with him on.
